S1.name: generated:S1
S1.description:
Forged/unsigned governed tap performs no payment and queues no write intent

risk: safety_invariant (priority P0)
purpose: Prove an unauthenticated caller cannot cause a governed carrier-invoice effect: a Slack /slack/actions POST carrying a governed-approval-shaped token but no valid HMAC signature must be refused before any governed handling, leaving zero payment effect and zero queued write intent in the durable store.
requirement: no payment effect occurs without a recorded approval
product principle: outcome_verification
rationale: The whole feature's safety hinge is that only an authenticated, recorded approval can advance the pipeline; a forged tap is the single most likely real-world attack and must land nothing.

S2.name: generated:S2
S2.description:
Two simultaneous forged governed taps do not race into a double effect

risk: concurrency (priority P0)
purpose: Issue two identical forged governed taps at the same instant and confirm the persisted store still shows zero completed governed writes and zero queued intents — no race turns two refusals into one (or two) effects.
requirement: an approved invoice is paid exactly once
product principle: outcome_verification
rationale: 'Paid exactly once' is a concurrency property; the classic failure is two near-simultaneous approvals both landing, so the race must be exercised, not assumed.

S4.name: generated:S4
S4.description:
Restart of the callback service fabricates no governed effect and leaves the audit store intact

risk: restart_recovery (priority P1)
purpose: Restart the callback service, then send one forged governed tap, and confirm: the security_events store is still queryable (durable), zero governed writes were completed (restart did not fabricate an effect or auto-resume anything), and the service is still fail-closed after restart.
requirement: approval survives a restart
product principle: failure_recovery
rationale: A restart is where in-memory grant handles are deliberately dropped; the durable decision store must survive and the process must not resurrect or invent an effect on the way back up.

generated at 2026-08-10T05:16:43+00:00 (stage=initial, wave 1)
because of risk: A restart could replay a durable queue into an executed write, or drop the audit store, so a governed effect appears (or an approval record vanishes) with no human in the loop.
